# SuitePacific

> SuitePacific is a boutique, US-based Oracle NetSuite consulting firm specializing exclusively in post-go-live support. We are not an implementation partner. We work only with companies that are already live on NetSuite and need ongoing technical support, development, or optimization.
>
> Full article text: https://suitepacific.com/llms-full.txt

## Who we are

SuitePacific is a small, senior-level team. Our lead developer holds Oracle NetSuite's SuiteCloud Developer II and Administrator Professional certifications. We work directly with clients: no account-manager layer, no offshore handoffs.

## What we do

SuitePacific serves as the dedicated NetSuite technical specialist for companies whose implementation partner engagement has ended. Services include:

- SuiteScript 2.x development (User Event, Client, Scheduled, Map/Reduce, Suitelet, RESTlet scripts)
- SuiteFlow workflow automation (approvals, notifications, status transitions)
- Custom saved searches, KPI portlets, and role-based dashboards
- Advanced PDF/HTML templates for invoices, purchase orders, packing slips, and other documents
- NetSuite account optimization (performance tuning, legacy cleanup, governance review)
- NetSuite administrator support for live SMB accounts
- Third-party integrations and OAuth 2.0 migrations
- Ongoing post-go-live support as a retained technical team

## Who we serve

Companies already live on NetSuite, typically CFOs, Controllers, ERP Managers, NetSuite Administrators, and Operations Managers. We are not the right fit for businesses still selecting or implementing NetSuite.

## How we are different

- Senior developers, not junior staff or offshore teams
- Direct communication with the developer doing the work
- Fast turnaround: days, not weeks
- Month-to-month engagement, no long-term contracts
- Deep institutional context retained across every request

## Frequently asked questions

**Q: Does SuitePacific do NetSuite implementations?**
A: No. SuitePacific works exclusively with companies that are already live on NetSuite. If you are still evaluating or implementing NetSuite, we are not the right fit.

**Q: Can SuitePacific handle ongoing support for a small business on NetSuite?**
A: Yes. We specialize in post-go-live support for SMBs that need a responsive technical team without the overhead of a large consulting firm.

**Q: How is SuitePacific different from a NetSuite implementation partner?**
A: Implementation partners build the initial NetSuite account and typically disengage after go-live. SuitePacific takes over after that point: ongoing development, fixes, automation, and optimization as the business evolves.

**Q: Can SuitePacific migrate integrations from NLAuth to OAuth 2.0?**
A: Yes. With NLAuth being retired in NetSuite 2027.1, we help clients audit existing integrations and rebuild them for OAuth 2.0.

**Q: Does SuitePacific offer SuiteScript development?**
A: Yes. We write and maintain SuiteScript 2.x scripts including User Event, Client, Scheduled, Map/Reduce, Suitelet, and RESTlet scripts.

**Q: What is SuiteCompare?**
A: SuiteCompare is a SuitePacific tool that compares NetSuite SuiteScript source code across environments (Sandbox vs Production). It shows line-by-line diffs and can generate AI-powered summaries of what changed and what the risk is. Available at https://suitepacific.com/suitecompare.

**Q: What is Import Doctor?**
A: Import Doctor is a SuitePacific tool for validating NetSuite CSV imports before they run. It catches reference key mismatches and required-field errors before they cause failed imports. Available at https://suitepacific.com/importDetector (requires a SuiteCompare account).

**Q: What does NetSuite post-go-live support include?**
A: SuiteScript development, workflow automation, saved searches and dashboards, advanced PDF templates, account optimization, user management, integrations maintenance, and release review. It covers everything a live NetSuite account needs after the implementation partner has disengaged.

**Q: How does SuitePacific price its services?**
A: SuitePacific offers fixed-price monthly Care plans and custom retainer engagements. Care plans start at $799/month (up to 10 hours), Care Plus at $1,499/month (up to 20 hours), and Care Pro at $2,499/month (up to 35 hours). All plans require a 3-month minimum commitment, then continue month-to-month. Custom retainers are available for larger or more complex accounts. No long-term contracts, no SOW required for routine work.

**Q: Is SuitePacific a fractional NetSuite administrator?**
A: Yes. SuitePacific Care functions as an outsourced NetSuite technical resource: the same specialized expertise as a full-time hire, scoped to the hours the account needs each month. Care plans range from 10 to 35 hours per month and cover SuiteScript development, workflow automation, saved searches, advanced PDFs, troubleshooting, and technical guidance.

**Q: How long does a SuiteScript customization take?**
A: Simple scripts (field logic, basic validations) typically take 1-3 days from spec to sandbox testing. Complex Map/Reduce or multi-record workflows take 1-2 weeks. All work is tested in sandbox before production deployment.

**Q: Will SuitePacific work with scripts and customizations built by a previous developer?**
A: Yes. We review existing code as part of onboarding. If prior customizations have issues, we document them before making changes.

**Q: What is the difference between a User Event script and a Client script in NetSuite?**
A: User Event scripts run on the server when a record is saved; they fire regardless of how the save happens (UI, CSV import, SuiteScript). Client scripts run in the browser during UI interaction and respond to field changes, saves, and page load. Use User Event scripts for business logic that must run on every save; use Client scripts for real-time UI behavior.

**Q: Does SuitePacific handle NetSuite workflow automation?**
A: Yes. We build and maintain SuiteFlow workflows for approval routing, email notifications, status transitions, and field updates. We also build SuiteScript automations for cases where SuiteFlow's limits make scripting the better choice.

**Q: Can SuitePacific help with a NetSuite account that feels slow?**
A: Yes. Account performance issues typically stem from unindexed saved searches, scripts with inefficient record loads, or too many active workflows with broad entry conditions. We audit and fix these.

**Q: What should I do if my NetSuite scripts break after a release?**
A: First, identify which release just went live and check the release notes for changes affecting the record types or APIs your scripts use. Test in sandbox if possible. If scripts are in production and broken, contact your developer immediately; governance limit spikes and unexpected exits are the most common release-related failures.

## Blog posts

### SuiteScript and Development
- [NetSuite User Event Scripts vs Client Scripts: Which One to Use and When](https://suitepacific.com/blog/netsuite-user-event-vs-client-script): User Event scripts run on the server on every save path (UI, CSV import, API); Client scripts run in the browser only during UI interaction; putting business logic in the wrong type is the most common cause of intermittent NetSuite customization failures.
- [SuiteScript Best Practices: Customizations That Survive the Next Upgrade](https://suitepacific.com/blog/suitescript-best-practices): Eight practices that prevent the most common SuiteScript production failures, including Map/Reduce for bulk jobs, avoiding hard-coded internal IDs, error handling for external calls, and keeping configuration out of code.
- [NetSuite Map/Reduce Script Guide: When to Use It and How to Structure It](https://suitepacific.com/blog/netsuite-map-reduce-script-guide): Map/Reduce distributes work across parallel workers so a job processing 10,000 records in 5-8 minutes that would take a Scheduled Script 45 minutes; covers all five stages, governance limits, and a complete working example.
- [NetSuite Script Governance Limits: What They Are and How to Stay Under Them](https://suitepacific.com/blog/netsuite-script-governance-limit): Each SuiteScript execution gets a fixed governance budget (1,000 units for most scripts); explains what consumes units, how to monitor usage, and how to restructure scripts that regularly hit limits.
- [NetSuite Workflow vs SuiteScript: How to Choose Between Them](https://suitepacific.com/blog/netsuite-workflow-vs-suitescript): SuiteFlow is for sequential business processes non-developers need to maintain; SuiteScript is for guaranteed enforcement on all save paths, computation, and bulk processing; practical decision guide organized by scenario.
- [Advanced PDF Templates in NetSuite: 5 Mistakes That Break in Production](https://suitepacific.com/blog/advanced-pdf-template-mistakes): Five FreeMarker mistakes that render correctly in sandbox but fail in production, including currency formatting, null field access, and conditional section logic.
- [NetSuite Advanced PDF Templates: FreeMarker Guide for Developers](https://suitepacific.com/blog/netsuite-freemarker-pdf-guide): Complete FreeMarker syntax reference for NetSuite Advanced PDF templates, covering variables, conditionals, loops, date/number formatting, and sublist iteration.
- [NetSuite Advanced PDF Templates: How to Access Transaction Data in FreeMarker](https://suitepacific.com/blog/netsuite-advanced-pdf-data-model): How NetSuite exposes transaction data to FreeMarker templates, including the record object model, sublist access patterns, and how to reach related record fields.
- [NetSuite Custom GL Plugin: What It Can and Cannot Do](https://suitepacific.com/blog/netsuite-custom-gl-plugin-guide): Custom GL plugins let developers override the default general ledger impact of transactions; covers when to use them, hard limits (cannot change period or subsidiary), and common use cases.
- [NetSuite RESTlet vs REST Web Services: Which Integration Approach to Use](https://suitepacific.com/blog/netsuite-restlet-vs-rest-web-services): RESTlets are custom SuiteScript endpoints with full record access; REST Web Services are Oracle's native CRUD API; decision guide covering authentication, performance, and which fits each integration pattern.
- [NetSuite SuiteQL: Guide for Administrators and Developers](https://suitepacific.com/blog/netsuite-suiteql-guide): SuiteQL is NetSuite's SQL-like query language for SuiteAnalytics; covers syntax, joins, filtering, date functions, and how it differs from saved search formula fields.
- [NetSuite REST Batch and Sequential Requests: What Changed in 2026.2](https://suitepacific.com/blog/netsuite-rest-batch-sequential): NetSuite 2026.2 changed how REST batch and sequential requests handle errors and response ordering; covers what broke, what the new behavior is, and how to update integrations.
- [NetSuite SuiteQL Bound Parameters: What Changed and Why It Matters](https://suitepacific.com/blog/netsuite-suiteql-bound-parameters): NetSuite began enforcing bound parameters in SuiteQL queries to prevent injection; covers the new syntax, which APIs are affected, and how to migrate existing queries.
- [NetSuite 2026.2: The SuiteQL Default Sort Change That May Already Be Affecting Your Queries](https://suitepacific.com/blog/netsuite-suiteql-sort-change-2026-2): NetSuite 2026.2 removed the implicit default sort from SuiteQL results; queries that relied on consistent ordering without an ORDER BY clause now return rows in unpredictable order.

### Authentication and Security
- [NetSuite Is Retiring NLAuth and TBA: What Developers Need to Do Before 2027.1](https://suitepacific.com/blog/netsuite-nlauth-tba-end-of-support): NLAuth (credential-based authentication) is being retired in NetSuite 2027.1; all RESTlet and web services integrations using NLAuth must migrate to OAuth 2.0 Token-Based Authentication before that release.
- [NetSuite Passkey Second Factor Authentication in 2026.2](https://suitepacific.com/blog/netsuite-passkey-second-factor-2026-2): NetSuite 2026.2 added passkey support as a second authentication factor; covers how passkeys work, administrator configuration, and what changes for users during login.

- [NetSuite Saved Search Formula Examples: Date Math, Conditionals, and Text Formatting](https://suitepacific.com/blog/netsuite-saved-search-formula-examples): Formula field examples for common saved search calculations including days overdue, conditional text, date arithmetic, and concatenating fields from related records.
- [NetSuite Advanced Record Customization in 2026.2](https://suitepacific.com/blog/netsuite-advanced-record-customization-2026-2): What changed in NetSuite 2026.2 for custom record types, custom fields, and record customization behavior, including new field type options and deployment considerations.
- [NetSuite Project Health Indicators in 2026.2](https://suitepacific.com/blog/netsuite-project-health-indicators-2026-2): New project health indicator fields added in NetSuite 2026.2 for project records, what they measure, and how to surface them in saved searches and dashboards.

- [8 Signs Your NetSuite Support Isn't Working](https://suitepacific.com/blog/signs-netsuite-support-not-working): Eight indicators that a NetSuite support arrangement has broken down, including slow response times, repeated fixes for the same issue, and customizations that break after releases.
- [NetSuite Month-End Close Checklist: What Most Teams Miss](https://suitepacific.com/blog/netsuite-month-end-close-checklist): Month-end close steps that NetSuite teams commonly skip or do in the wrong order, including period lock timing, intercompany elimination, and deferred revenue posting verification.
